elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence in Section 1.4: "Upon written notice to HDI identifying the entity, the Company's affiliates (any entity controlling, controlled by, or under common control with the Company) may exercise the Company's rights of access and use under this Section 1.4." "Company" is defined in the preamble as The Deerskin Companies, Inc. only, so this insertion (not duplication) is what supplies affiliate coverage.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: Neither Section 1.4 as rendered nor the inserted sentence mentions contractors, agents or service providers acting on the Company's behalf; the grant runs to the Company and (as amended) its affiliates only. To meet this element the drafter would need to add "and contractors acting on the Company's behalf" to the persons who may exercise the Section 1.4 access and use rights.

Condition does not apply: Section 1.4 grants term-based access to HDI's hosted system and administration tools under a fee-bearing hosting arrangement; there is no paid-up (fully-paid, one-time-fee) licence anywhere in the cited operative language for perpetuity to attach to.

Condition does not apply for the same reason: no paid-up licence exists under this hosting agreement, so there is no fully-paid grant that could be made irrevocable. Separately, nothing in Section 1.4 makes the access right revocable at HDI's discretion, so walk-away territory is not engaged.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: The Section 1.4 access and use right is term/subscription-style, but neither the original nor the redlined text limits HDI's ability to end it to the Company's uncured material breach; no such restriction was added. Defect to repair: add operative words such as "HDI may suspend or terminate the access and use rights granted in this Section 1.4 only upon the Company's material breach that remains uncured after written notice and a cure period."

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: Section 10.3 (retained unchanged): "This Agreement shall be binding upon, and shall inure to the benefit of and be enforceable by, the parties hereto and their respective legal representatives, successors and assigns" — successors take and may enforce the Company's rights, and no HDI-consent precondition appears in the cited assignment language.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: The insertion expressly conditions affiliate exercise on notice: "Upon written notice to HDI identifying the entity, the Company's affiliates ... may exercise the Company's rights of access and use under this Section 1.4." The written-notice trigger and the control-based affiliate definition are both supplied, so the mechanic is not left undefined.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: Already met by retained Section 10.3, under which the Agreement inures to the benefit of and is enforceable by the parties' "successors and assigns" with no consent gate; a successor by merger or acquisition therefore takes the Section 1.4 rights. No edit was needed or made here.

reasons: Fallback level is complete on the operative text: affiliate coverage is created by the single inserted sentence in Section 1.4 with an express written-notice trigger and a self-contained control-based affiliate definition, and successor transfer is already carried by retained Section 10.3.

Preferred level is incomplete: contractors acting on the Company's behalf are not added to the grant, and no limit confining termination of the Section 1.4 subscription-style access right to uncured material breach was inserted. The paid-up perpetual/irrevocable elements are vacuously satisfied because this hosting agreement contains no fully-paid licence.

Minimality holds. "Company" is defined as The Deerskin Companies, Inc. alone, so affiliates were genuinely absent and the addition is not duplicative coverage. The drafter added one sentence, took nothing out (no deletion of favourable or unrelated wording), added no survival tail, expense, remedy or procedure language, and correctly did not add a separate personnel/access edit or a broad "notwithstanding" override where a direct grant-of-exercise sentence suffices.

Intent is preserved: the insertion is drafted as affiliates exercising "the Company's rights" under Section 1.4 rather than as an independent grant, so it does not squarely contradict the retained tail of Section 10.3 ("no other person shall acquire or have any rights under this Agreement"), and it leaves timing, bandwidth, capacity and administration-tool mechanics untouched. Optional hardening if HDI pushes back: append "(without acquiring rights independent of the Company)" or a short cross-reference so the Section 10.3 third-party limitation cannot be read against the affiliate exercise right — not required for completeness at the fallback.

Classification as a deviation is supportable only because the fallback affiliate element failed pre-redline with no path to add affiliates; note in negotiation that the grant is not revocable at HDI's discretion, so this was never walk-away territory.
